tagline: Along the Gulf past dune lakes, old Grayton and newer Seaside.
intro: County Road 30A leaves US 98 west of Santa Rosa Beach and bends down to the Gulf, a two-lane road keeping near the shore for some 24 miles through Walton County before it rejoins the highway near Inlet Beach. It crosses coastal dune lakes, cuts through stretches of Point Washington State Forest and Deer Lake State Park, and passes a dozen beach communities, with the paved Timpoochee Trail running parallel to the Gulf.
Summer people found this shore in the 1890s, and beach lots went on sale in the 1920s. Grayton Beach came first, settled in 1885 by an Army major, Charles T. Gray, on ground too sandy to farm.

moments.title: Grayton Beach
moments.text: The shore's first village and, in 1913, its first resort, with narrow tree-lined streets and a general store, at the middle of a 20-mile run of coastal dune lakes.

moments.title: Seaside
moments.text: Built from 1981 to look like an old-fashioned Panhandle beach town of wood-framed cottages, and made over in 1998 as the set of The Truman Show.

moments.title: Deer Lake State Park
moments.text: A wooden boardwalk leads through tall sand dunes to the beach, in a park the road crosses for about three miles.
